newsitem.title: CHINA: New China field seen producing 5,900 barrels a day.
newsitem.headline: New China field seen producing 5,900 barrels a day.

text.p: A new oil field in the South China Sea is capable of producing 5,900 barrels of crude a day, the China News Service said on Thursday.
The Huizhou 32-5 field, located 172 km southeast of Hong Kong, was discovered by the the China Offshore Oil Nan Hai East Corp (CONHE) and the ACT OG consortium, the China Daily said.

The field was the fifth discovered in the Pearl River basin by CONHE and the ACT OG consortium, which groups Italy's Agip (Overseas) Ltd, Chevron Overseas Petroleum Ltd, a subsidiary of Chevron, and Texaco Petroleum Maatschappij (Nederland) BV, a subsidiary of U.S. giant Texaco, it said.
Development prospects for the field were considerable, the China News Service said, but gave no other details.
